column16: Net migration
column17: The number of immigrants minus the number of emigrants. Positive values mean more people moved into the country than left it.

column16: Net migration rate
column17: The number of immigrants minus the number of emigrants, per 1,000 people in the population. Positive values mean more people moved into the country than left it.

column16: Asylum seekers by country of origin
column17: [People](#dod:asylumseeker) who fled their country of origin and are in need of international protection, but have not yet been granted asylum in any country.
column18: This data includes all asylum-seekers, not just those who fled or applied for asylum that year.

column16: Asylum seekers by country of origin per 100,000 people
column17: [People](#dod:asylumseeker) who fled their country of origin and are in need of international protection, but have not yet been granted asylum in any country. This is given as the rate of asylum seekers per 100,000 people living in the origin country.
column18: This data includes all asylum-seekers, not just those who fled or applied for asylum that year.

column16: Asylum seekers by country they live in
column17: [People](#dod:asylumseeker) who fled their country of origin and are in need of international protection, but have not yet been granted asylum in the country. This includes all asylum seekers, not just those who applied for asylum that year.

column16: Asylum seekers by country they live in per 100,000 people
column17: [People](#dod:asylumseeker) who fled their country of origin and are in need of international protection, but have not yet been granted asylum in the country. This data is given per 100,000 people living in the country of asylum and shows the how many asylum seekers live in a country proportionate to its total population.
column18: This data includes all asylum-seekers who live in this country, not just those who arrived or applied for asylum that year.

column16: Refugees by country of origin
column17: [People](#dod:refugee) who fled their country of origin because of serious threats against which the authorities of their home country cannot or will not protect them. This includes all refugees, not just those who fled that year.

column16: Child refugees by country of origin
column17: Number of children under 18 years old who are [refugees](#dod:refugee) by their country of origin. This number describes all refugees who have left their origin country, not only refugees leaving in this year.

column16: Refugees by country of origin per 1,000 people
column17: [People](#dod:refugee) who fled their country of origin and are in need of international protection. This data is given per 1,000 people in their country of origin and shows how many people fled a country as a proportion of its current population.
column18: This data includes all refugees, not just those who fled that year.

column16: Child refugees by country of origin per 1000 inhabitants of all ages

column16: Returned refugees by country of origin

column16: Returned refugees by country they returned from

column16: Internally displaced people
column17: [Internally displaced people](#dod:internally-displaced) had to leave their homes because of violence or [disaster](#dod:idmc-disaster) and have not crossed an international state border. This counts all individuals who are currently displaced, regardless of how many times they have been displaced.
column18: A value of 0 means that IDMC is not aware of any internally displaced people (IDPs) in that region at the time of reporting. It does not mean that IDMC has confirmed that there are no IDPs.

column16: Total internal displacements
column17: [Internal displacements](#dod:displacements) due to both conflict and violence and [disaster](#dod:idmc-disaster). Internal displacement describes the movement of a person who is forced to leave their home but who remains within their country's borders. One person can be displaced multiple times within a calendar year and is then counted multiple times in the data.

column16: Stateless people by country they live in
column17: [People](#dod:stateless) who are not considered nationals of any state, by the country they live in. A person can be born stateless due to unknown parentage, discrimination against minority groups or complex nationality laws or become stateless by losing their nationality.

column16: Stateless people by country they live in, per 100,000 people
column17: [People](#dod:stateless) who are not considered nationals of any state, by the country they live in. This data is given per 100,000 inhabitants and shows the how many stateless people live in a country proportionate to its total population. A person can be stateless for many reasons, including (among others) unknown parentage, discrimination or complex nationality laws.
